wins: Mapped external perimeter services and recorded open ports, yielding initial situational awareness in <5 minutes.
Captured detailed service banners that can be reused for future credential bruteforce attempts, contributing to the 47.5 reward.
fails: Failed to escalate privileges after initial compromise; no flags or critical assets were exfiltrated.
Maintained a 0% success rate due to inability to chain post-recon footholds into a definitive exploit.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was efficient and informative, but follow-on exploitation and privilege escalation were not achieved, leaving the kill chain incomplete.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Post-recon exploitation attempts stall because the chosen service does not accept promoted payloads or credentials from initial scans.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 is open with HTTP banner indicating outdated WordPress or CMS
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted HTTP enumeration (wpscan and nikto) and gather plugin versions

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open with a weak banner or default credentials suspected
skill_cards.then_action: Launch credential spray using hydra and capture key exchange for later replay

skill_cards.if_condition: When initial recon identifies a Linux host with a known misconfiguration (e.g., world-writable cron)
skill_cards.then_action: Implement automated loop to test for writable cron/job files and schedule a reverse shell payload

memory_ops.reason: Effective reconnaissance of HTTP services led to actionable intelligence early in the run.
SSH enumeration showed promise; capturing banners and brute-force attempts provided structured data.

next_experiments.title: Credential reuse pivot
next_experiments.description: Take low-barrier credentials discovered on an exposed service and attempt to reuse them across additional internal hosts via SSH and SMB.

next_experiments.title: Automated post-exploit staging
next_experiments.description: Develop a scripted post-compromise routine that checks for sudo misconfigurations and world-writable cron entries immediately after initial access.

next_experiments.title: Web shell persistence trial
next_experiments.description: Deploy a non-destructive web shell on the identified web app and validate persistence while monitoring defensive detections.
